# Docker testing

Every package is tested twice:

1. **Unit tests** against local mock HTTP servers (no network, no Docker), with coverage gates:
   TypeScript, Python and Java ≥ 90 % lines and branches, Rust ≥ 90 % lines and regions, Go ≥ 90 %
   statements.
2. **Integration tests** against a real `__IMAGE__` in Docker. The package is **packed and installed
   into a separate consumer project** first, so the suite imports it exactly like a user does.

## Run the integration suite

```sh
make test-docker                      # all five languages
make test-docker LANGS="go python"    # a subset
```

What happens per language:

1. `docker/compose.yml` starts __DISPLAY__ (`__IMAGE__`) and waits for its health check.
2. A one-shot `bootstrap` container prepares it (users, tokens, …) and writes the credentials to
   `/bootstrap/env` (`KEY=value` lines) on a shared volume.
3. The `test-<lang>` image (built from `docker/Dockerfile.<lang>` with the repo root as context)
   builds and packs the package, installs it into `<lang>/integration/` and runs the integration
   tests plus the **conformance runner** with `GROW___KEY_UPPER___URL` pointing at the service.
4. The stack is always removed with `docker compose down -v`, also on failure or Ctrl-C.

Every run uses its own Compose project name and publishes **no host ports**, so runs can happen in
parallel on one machine.

## Conformance scenarios

`conformance/scenarios/*.json` hold language-neutral scenarios. Each language's runner executes
the scenarios of this service's categories against the real service and reports skipped scenarios
with the reason:

- `core.health` — health, ping, server version, close
<!-- @sdk-kit:if secrets -->
- `secrets.*` — round trip, bulk reads, missing secrets, redaction
<!-- @sdk-kit:endif -->
<!-- @sdk-kit:if logging -->
- `logging.*` — round trip, batching, redaction
<!-- @sdk-kit:endif -->
<!-- @sdk-kit:if tracing -->
- `tracing.*` — span tree, services
<!-- @sdk-kit:endif -->

Unit-level conformance (retries, timeouts, redaction, close twice) is covered by unit tests named
after the ids in `conformance/core-unit.md`.

## Test fakes for your own tests

Each package ships in-memory fakes so your application tests need neither Docker nor network:

| Language | Module |
| - | - |
| TypeScript | `@grow-codes/__KEY__/testing` |
| Rust | `grow___KEY_SNAKE__::testing` (feature `testing`) |
| Go | `github.com/grow-codes-packages/__KEY__/go/testkit` |
| Python | `grow___KEY_SNAKE__.testing` |
| Java | `codes.grow.packages.__PKG__.testing` |

## CI

The `ci` workflow runs the unit pipelines (TypeScript on Node 22 and 24, Rust stable and 1.88,
Go 1.26 and 1.27, Python 3.10, 3.13 and 3.14, Java 17, 21 and 25) and one Docker integration job
per language. Failed Docker jobs upload the Compose logs as the artifact `compose-logs-<lang>`.
